text:
miguel: heads-up — customer acme-inc on Dedicated pool eu-west-2-prod-3 opened a ticket: sudden throughput drop (~50%) + elevated p50/p95 and intermittent 429s. Not a model change on their side AFAIK.

anya: thanks — ticket id? any recent deploys to that pool?

miguel: TICKET-8432. last deploy to runtime was ~03:10 UTC (canary) but rollback showed no change. attaching first logs: 
```
2026-03-17T03:28:12Z INF request id=... tenant=acme path=/v1/generate tokens=1 latency_ms=4200
2026-03-17T03:28:13Z ERR throttle 429 tenant=acme reason="rate_limit" batch_sz=1
2026-03-17T03:28:13Z DBG queue_depth=127 continuous-batcher window_ms=5
```

evan: seeing the same from the metrics side — continuous-batcher queue-depth spike around 03:26, but pack size collapsed to lots of single-token microbatches. looks like a surge of very small requests.

sre-bot: [ALERT] dedicated-pool eu-west-2-prod-3 throughput-drop severity=high triggered at 2026-03-17T03:27:50Z — metric names: infer_tokens/s, batch_fill_ratio, scheduler_queue_depth.

lina: any sign of KV cache churn or prefix cache misses? small requests + no cache hits could amplify load.

evan: prefix cache hit-rate for acme is 12% (normally ~72%). KV cache eviction spikes at same time — likely many unique short prompts.

support-engineer: customer says they added a client-side streaming wrapper that splits longer prompts into many 1-3 token calls to get partial outputs. They only started this morning.

anya: ok that explains the microbatching. two-pronged ask: (1) short term mitigation to restore throughput, (2) longer term guards so noisy tenant doesn't impact other tenants.

miguel: short-term ideas I can try now: bump max_batch_tokens to 4096 on the pool, increase batch_window_ms from 5 -> 15 for this pool, and enable tenant_smoothing=on (experimental) to coalesce tiny requests. can also move acme to spare pool with burst capacity if needed.

evan: note: increasing batch_window will add ~10-25ms tail latency — customer expects lower latency but they reported p95 spikes already. tradeoff seems acceptable to regain overall throughput.

lina: we should also check autoscaler behaviour — looks like autoscaler didn't spin up extra replicas because pool was at reserved_capacity cap. running `redwoodctl autoscale describe eu-west-2-prod-3` -> shows cap=10 and current=10.

miguel: good catch. support-engineer can we ask customer if they have Dedicated burst credits? otherwise ops can temporarily raise reserved_capacity to 12 for 30m.

support-engineer: asking now.

anya: longer term — add a heuristic to scheduler: if batch_fill_ratio < 0.25 and avg_batch_tokens < threshold for >1m, treat as noisy-tenant mode and apply per-tenant smoothing + rate-limiter. file a ticket for scheduler rule.

evan: also want to log tenant-level microbatching patterns into observability so we can alert before global impact.

miguel: repro path for eng: we can replay a small-client flood using `tools/traffic_replay/replayer --pcap acme-flood.pcap --rate 2000` against a staging pool with current scheduler config. includes script to simulate streaming-chunked client.

miguel: running mitigation now: (1) bumped batch_window_ms to 15 on eu-west-2-prod-3 (2) increased max_batch_tokens to 4096 (3) temporarily raised reserved_capacity to 12. will monitor.

sre-bot: [ACTION] applied config change batch_window_ms=15 to eu-west-2-prod-3 by miguel at 2026-03-17T03:32:05Z.

evan: after change — queue_depth down from 127 -> 24, batch_fill_ratio improved from 0.12 -> 0.6, throughput recovering. p95 reduced but still above baseline.

support-engineer: acme confirms latency improved and 429s dropped. they're rolling back the streaming wrapper for now.

anya: next steps: (1) eng-runtime to implement noisy-tenant detection + per-tenant smoothing ticket ENG-6152, (2) ops to add autoscaler override runbook for reserved_capacity short-term increases, (3) add observability dashboard for per-tenant microbatch metrics.

miguel: I'll open ENG-6152 and assign to evan + lina. leaving the config changes until morning unless acme asks us to revert.

lina: also worth auditing recent scheduler tune PRs from last week; even if rollback didn't help, we should ensure no regressions slipped into config.

miguel: thanks all. tagging @oncall for visibility. :white_check_mark:
